:JUDGMENT:
This is a Petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the death of Miss.Himadri Sharma D/o Shivanarayana Sharma in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. Brief averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 25-03-2022 at about 2.45 p.m., while Himadri Sharma (deceased) was riding the Scooter bearing no.KA-02-KL- 9273 on NH-4 from Jalahalli Cross towards Guruguntepalya under Metro station, a Goods vehicle bearing no.KA-52-A-2609 driven by its driver at high-speed in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed against the deceased.
Consequently, she fell-down and sustained grievous-injuries.
She was immediately shifted to Prakriya Hospital, wherein she was declared as dead.
3. That prior to accident, Himadri Sharma was hale and healthy.
She was working as an Editor and News Correspondent with International and Indian Magazines and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
4. That the sole cause of the accident is the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods vehicle.
Hence Respondent no.1 being the insurer and Respondent no.2 being the owner of the Goods vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Thus it is prayed to allow the petition.
5. Respondent no.1 & 2 have appeared through their counsel.
However, respondent No.1 alone has filed the Objections Statement.
6. In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.1- Insurance Company has denied the petition-averments.
It has specifically denied that the age, avocation and income of the deceased.

It has also denied the involvement of the Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-A-2609 in the alleged accident, and has contended that the Goods Vehicle has been intentionally implicated in collusion with the Driver, Owner.
However it has admitted the issuance of insurance in respect of the Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-A-2609.
Thus, it is prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

In support of the case of Petitioners, Petitioner no.1 has been examined as P.W.1 and Exs.P.1 to 39 have been marked.
Exs. P.1 to Ex.

P10 are the Police Documents viz., certified-copy of FIR,
Complaint, Spot Sketch, Inquest, Mahazar, Notice under Section 133 of MV Act, Reply to Notice,
Police Intimation, P.M. Report, IMV Report and Charge sheet.

14. The FIR & Complaint at Exs.P.1 & 2 show that the case has been registered against the driver of the offending Goods vehicle bearing no.KA-52-A-2609 for the offence punishable under Section 279, 304A of IPC.
Exs.P.3 and 4 are the Sketch and Mahazar respectively which show the accident spot.
Ex.P.5 is the Notice issued under Section 133 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.6 is Reply to said Notice given by the Owner of the Goods vehicle.
Ex.P.7 is the Police intimation.
Ex.P.8 is the P.M. Report which shows the cause of death is due to 'traumatic shock, multiple injuries sustained and blunt and hard force impact'.
Ex.P.9 is the IMV report which shows that the cause of accident is not due to any mechanical defects of the motor vehicles.
Ex.P.10 is the Charge sheet filed against the driver of the Goods vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304A of IPC and Section 134 A & B r/w Section 187 of MV Act.
The Medical bills and Prescriptions are at Exs.P.9 & 10.
Ex.P.11 is death certificate.
Exs. P.12 to 14 are notarized-copy of Aadhar card of petitioners and deceased.
15. Among these documents, the Spot Sketch at Ex.P.3 and the IMV Report at Ex.P.9 are vital to appreciate the factum of 'negligence'.
Admittedly, the accident has taken- place under the Metro Station

. A perusal of the Sketch at Ex.P.3 shows that the driver of the Goods Vehicle bearing no.KA-52-A- 2609 has taken his vehicle slightly to the left, due to which its left-side centre body portion has dashed against the Scooter of Himadri going on the left-side; and due to the impact,
Himadri has fallen to her right and has come under the Goods vehicle that has run over her.
This clearly is the result of 'negligence' on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The fact that the left-side centre body portion has dashed against the Scooter of Himadri is corroborated by the IMV Report at Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned that "Left-side Centre Body Portion at bottom base body of MV (Goods Vehicle bearing no.KA-52-A-2609) dented due to the impact"; and it is also mentioned that "the Right-side rear fender body of the MV (Scooter of Himadri) dented due to impact, right-side front fender and foot-rest of the MV damaged".

Further, the fact that Himadri Sharma has died due to the head-injury sustained in the accident is clear from the P.M.Report at Ex.P.8.
16.
On the other hand, Respondent no.1-Insurance Company has examined the Driver of the offending Goods Vehicle bearing no.KA-52-A-2609 - Manjunath as RW.1, and its Legal Manager as RW.2.
As prayed by Respondent no.1, summons was issued to the Investigation Officer, who has been examined as RW.3.
He has appeared before the court and has produced the CCTV Footage of the accident spot in a C.D. which is marked as Ex.P.7.

He has deposed that in Ex.P.7, the accident has not been captured, but the passing of the offending-vehicle and the Scooter of the victim just before the accident could be seen.

sentences.text: RW.1 has deposed that he was driving the Goods vehicle on the left-side of road, when a Scooter tried to overtake his vehicle from left even though there was no space, and in the process got stuck under the rear wheel of the Goods vehicle.
As discussed above, Exs.P.3 & 9 falsify this version of RW.1.
However, RW.1 has admitted that the charge sheet has been filed against him.
He has admitted the Notice and Reply to the notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act as per Exs.P.5 & 6 respectively.
From the notice at Ex.P.5 it is clear that the Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-A-2609 has been involved in the accident; and that RW.1 was driving the same at the time of accident.

18. In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the rashness & negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Goods vehicle, has led to the death of Himadri Sharma.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative".
19. Issue No.1 and 3: Since these issues are interlinked, they are taken-up together for discussion to avoid repetition of facts.
As per the petition, petitioner no.1 is mother and petitioner no.2 is the brother of deceased Miss.Himadri Sharma.

In support of this fact, the Aadhar cards of petitioner no.1 & 2 at Exs.P.13 &
14 have been produced.
The Death Certificate at Ex.P.11 shows that petitioner no.1 is the mother of deceased Himadri Sharma.
The relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased is thus proved.
Moreover, there is no dispute about the relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
Thus petitioner no.1 who is the mother and petitioner no.2 who is the brother, are the legal-representatives of deceased Himadri Sharma.
20. As per the petition, the deceased was aged about 23 years as on the date of accident.
The Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.12 shows the date of birth of deceased as 27.02.1999, and the accident has occurred on 25.03.2022.
Thus deceased Himadri Sharma was aged about 23 years as on the date of accident.
21. Next, as per the petition, the deceased was working as Magazine Editor and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
Petitioners have not produced any document to prove the occupation and income of deceased.

However, the petitioners have produced the Marks Card, Degree Certificate,
Certificates of Appreciation and a few Course Certificates which shows that Himadri Sharma was a Graduate, Multi-talented Young Woman.
As per the Degree Certificate at Ex.P.19, she has obtained the Degree in Bachelor of Vocation - Visual Media & Film Making in the year 2019.
She has also done the Certificate Course in Advance Photography from the National Institute of Photography as per the Certificate at Ex.P.18.
She has also done Internships in various Newspaper Houses, has participated in various events and has obtained the Certificates of Appreciation which is evident from Exs.P.22 to 30.

She had Admission Offers from various Foreign Universities; and one such Admission Offer has been from the University of West Minister to pursue M.A., in Documentary Photography and Photojournalism, as per Ex.P.37, but it is merely the admission offer and not Scholarship (as argued by the learned counsel for petitoners).
None of these documents prove that the deceased had the Income of Rs.1,00,000/- per month.

However from the documents referred-to above, there is no doubt that deceased Himadri Multi-talented Young Graduate with big dreams,
who would have definitely progressed in her career.

Such being the case, the question is, whether it Bharathi Sharma vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53603720/
5 would be proper to take the notional income as Rs.15,500/- per month as the income of the deceased, as per the guidelines (since the said accident has been occurred in the year 2022) issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

sentences.text: The answer is 'No' considering the Qualification and Talent of the deceased.

entities.text: 2013 ACJ 1403 - High Court of Delhi - Rajesh and others Vs. Rajbir Singh & others

sentences.text: In the above judgment at Sl.No.1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has laid emphasis on awarding just compensation; the other two judgments of cited by the learned counsel for petitioners pertains to the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

Here it would be apt to refer to decision reported in: 2024 ACJ 658 - Kumud Gupta & Another Vs. Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.,:
Quantum - Fatal accident - Deceased a girl, B.Tech (Computer Science) student - Claimants:

entities.text: 2024 ACJ 658 - Kumud Gupta & Another Vs. Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Parents - Tribunal awarded Rs.47,10,000/- which was reduced to Rs.30,54,000/- by the High Court - Apex Court held that High Court was justified in taking income at Rs.20,000/- per month, adding 40% of income for future prospects and deducting 50% for personal expenses.

In the above referred decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court, the deceased was a B.Tech Student whose income has been taken as Rs.20,000/- per month, and 40% of income has been added towards future prospects, by deducting 50% for personal expenses.

Whereas in the case on hand, deceased Himadri has graduated in the year 2019; and with her qualification, talent, she would have been earning not less than Rs.20,000/-
per month, which would have only increased with the passage of time.
Under the circumstances, it would be just & proper to take the Income of deceased Himadri as Rs.20,000/- per month and also award future prospects.
22. As discussed above, the deceased has left behind her mother-petitioner no.1 and brother-petitioner No.2 as her dependents.

As per the decision reported in AIR 2017 S.C. 5157 - National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others: The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that :
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rs.15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rs.40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-.

sentences.text: The said amount has to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years".
Petitioner no.1 who is the mother has lost love & affection of deceased.
Therefore, petitioner no.1 is entitled to a sum of Bharathi Sharma vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53603720/

23. Next, as per the detailed discussion made supra, the income of the deceased who is aged about 23 years, is taken as Rs.20,000/- per month.
And as per the principle laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 - Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another: the multiplier applicable is '18'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in the process of calculation of 'Loss of Dependency' per year, we get 20,000 x 18 x 12 = Rs.43,20,000/-
In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is bachelor/spinster, 50% of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards her personal and living expenses.
In the case on hand, petitioner no.1 and 2 are dependents of the deceased.
Hence 50% of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Accordingly, after deducting 50% of the amount towards her personal expenses out of Rs.43,20,000/- it comes to Rs.21,60,000/- .
Thus the 'Loss of Dependency' would be Rs.21,60,000/-

Accordingly, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,60,000/-
towards 'Loss of Dependency'.
24.
Next, as discussed above, the deceased would have definitely progressed in her Career.
Hence 40% of 'Loss of Dependency' would be Rs.8,64,000/- to which the petitioners are entitled-to, under the Head 'Future Prospects'.

25. Considering the above aspects, petitioners are entitled for total compensation as under :
1. Loss of Dependency Rs.21,60,000/-
2. Future Prospects Rs. 8,64,000/-

3 . Loss of Consortium Rs.44,000/-
4. Loss of Estate Rs.16,500/-
5. Funeral Expenses Rs.16,500/-
6. Total Rs.31,01,000/-
Thus, Petitioner no.1 is awarded the total compensation of Rs.31,01,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

26. Regarding Liability : As already discussed above, the petitioners have proved that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligence driving of the driver of Goods vehicle bearing KA-52-A-2609.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, Respondent no.1 being the insurer has to indemnify the insured, and it has to deposit the compensation amount with interest.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative & Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER The Petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.

A sum of Rs.31,01,000/- (Rupees Thirty-one Lakhs One Thousand only) is awarded as total compensation to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its payment.
Respondent no.1 shall deposit the compensation amount to the court within 60 days from the date of this judgment.
Petitioner no.1 is entitled to 70% of the total compensation amount awarded.

Petitioner no.2 is entitled to 30% out of the total compensation amount awarded.

Out of which 50% of the award amount is ordered to be released to Petitioner no.2 by way of E-Payment after proper identification, and the remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner no.2 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1,000/-.

23. Next, as per the detailed discussion made supra, the income of the deceased who is aged about 23 years, is taken as Rs.20,000/- per month.

ORDER The Petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
A sum of Rs.31,01,000/- (Rupees Thirty-one Lakhs One Thousand only) is awarded as total compensation to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its payment.

Office to draw the award accordingly.
